  - Blake is 18 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care

  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

Regarding Blake:
  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you, I need to understand your situation with your child or children. Let me ask you the first question:

**How old is your child?** 

Please let me know:
- Their age (in years)
- Or which age group they fall into:
  - **Under 16**
  - **16 to 19**
  - **20 or over**

If you have multiple children, I can assess each of them individually.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I have two children actually. Alex is 17 and Blake just turned 18. They both still live at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you assess the eligibility for both Alex and Blake.

Let me start by checking their situations:

**For Alex (age 17):**
Since Alex is 17, they fall into the 16-19 age group. I need to check if they're currently in education or training, as this affects eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or an approved training course?**

**For Blake (age 18):**
Since Blake is 18, they also fall into the 16-19 age group. Similarly, I need to check if they're currently in education or training.

**Is Blake currently in full-time education or an approved training course?**

Please let me know the status for each of them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Well, Alex is still in sixth form doing their A-levels, so yes, they're in full-time education.

Blake finished school last year though and isn't studying anymore - they've been looking for work but haven't found anything yet.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me navigate through the eligibility checks for both of them.

**For Alex:** Since they're 17 and in full-time education (A-levels in sixth form), let me proceed with their assessment.

**For Blake:** Since they're 18 and NOT in full-time education or training, they would fall into a different category. Let me check their situation.

Let me continue with the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to clarify Blake's situation a bit more:

**For Blake (age 18):** When Blake finished school last year and stopped studying, approximately how long ago was that? Specifically:
- Has it been **less than 20 weeks** since Blake left full-time education?
- Or has it been **more than 20 weeks**?

This is important because there's an extension period after leaving education that might affect eligibility.

In the meantime, let me proceed with Alex's assessment since they're clearly in full-time education:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! For **Alex**, I can see that A-levels are an approved qualification. Let me confirm a couple of details:

**For Alex:**
1. Are they studying A-levels on a **full-time basis** with at least 12 hours per week of supervised study? (I assume yes, since they're in sixth form)
2. Is Alex **not working full-time** (i.e., not in a full-time job)?

Once you confirm this, I can proceed to check if there are any other eligibility requirements for Alex.

And please do let me know about Blake's timeline - was it less than or more than 20 weeks since they left education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, Alex is doing full-time A-levels at sixth form - definitely more than 12 hours a week! And no, they're not working at all, just focusing on their studies.

As for Blake, they finished school last summer, so that would be... well over 20 weeks ago now. It's been nearly a year actually.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying! That's very helpful.

**For Alex:** Since they're doing full-time A-levels (approved education) and not working, let me continue with their assessment. I need to check a few more eligibility criteria:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! For **Alex**, since they're not working at all, they definitely meet this requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**For Alex:** Is Alex receiving any of these benefits in their own right?
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (as an individual claimant, not as a dependent)

(I assume no, but I need to confirm)

**For Blake:** Since Blake left education nearly a year ago (well over 20 weeks), they don't qualify for the extension period. They're 18 and not in education or training. This means Blake would not be eligible for Child Benefit.

Please confirm about Alex's benefits situation so I can complete their assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name - they're just a student living at home with us.

And okay, I understand about Blake - that makes sense since they're not studying anymore.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with Alex's assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**For Alex:** Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship at all?

(I assume no, since they're doing full-time A-levels in sixth form, but I need to confirm)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship - they're just doing their A-levels at sixth form.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with Alex's assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If not, please let me know:
- Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- Do you have pre-settled status (and if so, are you working, studying, actively seeking work, or have sufficient resources)?
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

For most people, the answer to the first question would be "yes" if you live in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for confirming that you normally live in the UK. Let me continue with Alex's assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means:
- You live with Alex, OR
- You contribute to their upkeep (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc.), OR
- You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement

Given that you mentioned Alex lives at home with you, I assume the answer is yes - you live with them and support them. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me and I support them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with Alex's assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**For Alex:** Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or who might be claiming?

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for them?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent) claiming for Alex?

Or are you the only person claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - I'm the only one.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**For Alex:** Now I need to check their living situation:

- Is Alex currently in hospital?
- Is Alex in care (local authority or other care)?
- Is Alex fostered?
- Or is Alex living normally at home with you?

Given that you mentioned Alex lives at home with you, I assume the answer is "living normally at home." Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is just living at home with me - nothing unusual about their living situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**For Alex:** This is the final question - is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?

In other words:
- The local council is not paying for their housing or upkeep, correct?

(I assume yes, since you're supporting them at home, but I need to confirm)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm the one supporting them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! Let me navigate to the final outcome for Alex:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I now have all the information I need to provide you with a final eligibility outcome. Let me summarize:

**Summary of your situation:**
- **Alex (age 17):** In full-time education (A-levels), not working, not receiving benefits, living at home with you, you're responsible for them, you're the only claimant, and the council is not paying for their support
- **Blake (age 18):** Not in full-time education or training, and left education nearly a year ago (well over 20 weeks ago)

Now let me provide you with the final eligibility determination:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Your Child Benefit Eligibility Results**

### **✅ Alex (age 17): ELIGIBLE**

**You can claim Child Benefit for Alex.** They meet all the eligibility requirements:
- In full-time approved education (A-levels)
- Not working full-time
- You live with them and support them
- You normally reside in the UK
- No other claimant
- Local council is not paying for them

### **❌ Blake (age 18): NOT ELIGIBLE**

**You cannot claim Child Benefit for Blake.** The reason is:
- Blake is no longer in full-time education or approved training
- Blake left education nearly a year ago, which is **beyond the 20-week extension period** that applies to young people who have recently left education
- Without being in approved education/training, 18-year-olds are not qualifying children

---

## **Next Steps for Alex**

To claim Child Benefit for Alex, you should:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Important note:** Be aware of the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year

Payments are typically made every 4 weeks.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit eligibility?

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit. They meet all the required criteria: (1) Age 17 falls within the 16-19 qualifying age group; (2) They are in full-time approved education (A-levels at sixth form, exceeding the 12 hours per week requirement); (3) They are not working full-time (not in paid work at all); (4) They are not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in their own right; (5) They are not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (6) You normally reside in the UK (Manchester); (7) You are responsible for Alex as they live with you and you support them; (8) You are the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (9) Alex is living normally at home (not in hospital, care, or fostered); (10) The local council is not paying towards their accommodation or maintenance.

Blake is not eligible for Child Benefit. Although they are 18 years old and fall within the 16-19 age group, they do not meet the qualifying criteria because: (1) They are not in full-time education or approved training (they finished school and are no longer studying); (2) They do not qualify for the extension period for those who recently left education, as they left nearly a year ago, which is well beyond the 20-week extension limit; (3) Without being in approved education/training or within the extension period, 18-year-olds are not qualifying children for Child Benefit purposes.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex, who is 17 and in full-time A-level education at sixth form. Alex meets all the eligibility requirements as a qualifying child. However, Blake, who is 18 and has not been in education or training for nearly a year, does not qualify for Child Benefit as they fall outside both the active education requirement and the extension period for recently-leavers (which lasts only 20 weeks)."
